name: Cursor (Anysphere)
tagline: Makers of Cursor, the AI code editor. Recruiter call, one or two ~60 min technical screens (practical, product-flavored coding; reportedly no AI help beyond autocomplete in the first screens), then a paid on-site project day or two working on a real problem with the team, plus a founder chat.
notes: By far the most reported phone-screen question is building a Merkle tree over a repository and using it to diff two snapshots (find added/modified/removed files, skip identical subtrees), sometimes with a focus on deterministic hashing. Also reported: a streaming Markdown code-fence parser (chunks split delimiters arbitrarily), a user/team/company notification rate limiter (new-grad backend), an in-memory transactional key-value store with a discussion of conflicting concurrent writes, and design rounds (CI/CD or cron job scheduler, versioned IDE settings). Interviewers care about clean, working code for a realistic editor/infra problem, pinning down the contract (ordering, hashing format, edge cases) before coding, reasoning about incremental/streaming behaviour and complexity, and, in the project day, whether you actually use and care about the product.
